verses.english: Linked Discourses 47.5
1. In Ambapālī’s Mango Grove
A Heap of the Unskillful
At Sāvatthī.
There the Buddha said:

verses.pali: “‘akusalarāsī’ti, bhikkhave, vadamāno pañca nīvaraṇe sammā vadamāno vadeyya.
verses.english: “Rightly speaking, mendicants, you’d call these five hindrances a ‘heap of the unskillful’.

verses.pali: Kevalo hāyaṁ, bhikkhave, akusalarāsi, yadidaṁ—pañca nīvaraṇā.
verses.english: For these five hindrances are entirely a heap of the unskillful.
What five?
The hindrances of sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.

verses.pali: ‘Akusalarāsī’ti, bhikkhave, vadamāno ime pañca nīvaraṇe sammā vadamāno vadeyya.
verses.english: Rightly speaking, you’d call these five hindrances a ‘heap of the unskillful’.

verses.pali: Kevalo hāyaṁ, bhikkhave, akusalarāsi, yadidaṁ—pañca nīvaraṇā.
verses.english: For these five hindrances are entirely a heap of the unskillful.

verses.pali: ‘Kusalarāsī’ti, bhikkhave, vadamāno cattāro satipaṭṭhāne sammā vadamāno vadeyya.
verses.english: Rightly speaking, you’d call these four kinds of mindfulness meditation a ‘heap of the skillful’.

verses.pali: Kevalo hāyaṁ, bhikkhave, kusalarāsi, yadidaṁ—cattāro satipaṭṭhānā.
verses.english: For these four kinds of mindfulness meditation are entirely a heap of the skillful.
What four?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …
They meditate observing an aspect of the mind …

verses.pali: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: They meditate observing an aspect of principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: ‘Kusalarāsī’ti, bhikkhave, vadamāno ime cattāro satipaṭṭhāne sammā vadamāno vadeyya.
verses.english: Rightly speaking, you’d call these four kinds of mindfulness meditation a ‘heap of the skillful’.

verses.pali: Kevalo hāyaṁ, bhikkhave, kusalarāsi, yadidaṁ—cattāro satipaṭṭhānā”ti.
verses.english: For these four kinds of mindfulness meditation are entirely a heap of the skillful.”
